title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche continuation, Grothendieck studies pairs (ξ,η) in Π̂_{0,3}×Π̂_{0,3} solving the system (133)(134). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite on two generators. The system has the GT-type shape ξ f(ξ) ρ²(η)=1, η ρ_∞(η)=1. He pushes solutions to SL(2,Ẑ) through the identification of Π_{0,3} with the level-2 congruence subgroup (whence the conditions ξ≡η≡1 mod 2). The previous page proved the relations (154)(155), with μ=2ν+1 invertible and determined by ξ.

This page is a 'Remarque' giving a full parametrisation of the image, step by step.
1. The constraints are AD−BC=1 and C+D−B=1, with D a unit. So ξ=[[A,B],[C,D]] is determined by (B,D).
2. Solution pairs (ξ,η) of the matrix system (156) correspond bijectively to pairs (B,D) with B∈Ẑ, B≡0 mod 2, and D∈Ẑ^*.
3. Formulas (157)(158): C=B−D+1, A=(1+BC)/D=μ(1+B+B²)−B, μ=1/D, ν=(μ−1)/2.
4. Normalising η=ξ l_1^{−ν}, with l_1^{−ν}=[[1,0],[−2ν,1]], gives (159): U=D, S=B, R=A−2νB=μ(1+B²)=(1+B²)/D.
5. Also T=C−2νD=B+1−μD=B, so η=[[(1+B²)/D, B],[B, D]] is a symmetric matrix of determinant 1.
6. (160): he sets u_ξ = μ[[1,B],[0,D]] = [[μ, μB],[0,1]] = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]] ∈ GL(2,Ẑ). This is an element of the affine ('ax+b') Borel group of Ẑ, with det u_ξ = μ.
7. Knowing u_ξ is equivalent to knowing ξ mod the congruence image, and equivalent to knowing the normalised pair (ξ,η). He compares with u_{α,β} on p. 398' (78).

Margin remarks:
- The congruence conditions are inessential; the algebraic statement holds without them.
- NB (161): μ=det u_ξ, and η=ξ l_1^{−ν}, ξ=η l_1^{ν}.

The next page interprets u_ξ as an automorphism of the 'abelianised' level-2 structure: u_ξ(σ_∞)=η, u_ξ(ρ)=ξ, u_ξ(ε_0)=ε_0^μ. It then shows that, among all u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ), the condition u(ε_0)=ε_0^μ together with det u=μ forces exactly the upper-triangular form [[μ,M],[0,1]] (when P=1).

Purpose: to determine the image in GL(2,Ẑ) (the linearised/modular shadow) of the GT-like automorphism group Aut^!_{0,3}. The answer is the affine group Ẑ ⋊ Ẑ^*.
errors: The relation written at top is read as A+D−B=1, but (157) uses C=B−D+1, i.e. C+D−B=1. The 'A' appears to be overwritten by 'C' in the manuscript; with A+D−B=1 the formula for A would not follow.
No mathematical error found. The computations of A, R, T and the determinant check out, including the unstated consequence T=B, which makes η symmetric.
Minor gap: ν=(μ−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ requires μ≡1 mod 2. This follows from D∈Ẑ^* being odd at 2, but it is not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: Explicit parametrisation of solutions of the GT-type equations, after reduction to SL(2,Ẑ) via the level-2 congruence image, by pairs (B,D) ∈ 2Ẑ × Ẑ^*.
ideas.modern_name: Image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (or of G_Q) in the automorphisms of the profinite congruence/abelian quotient of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}); linearised GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara, Nakamura and others for linear/metabelian images
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known; unsure

ideas.what: Packaging the solution into u_ξ = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]] ∈ GL(2,Ẑ), an affine-group element with determinant μ (the 'cyclotomic' exponent).
ideas.modern_name: Affine group Ẑ ⋊ Ẑ^* as the image of GT/G_Q in a Borel subgroup (analogue of the cyclotomic character plus a Kummer-type cocycle)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ihara's work on the action on the Fermat/abelian tower; Deligne)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to u_{α,β} on p. 398' of the same manuscript

ideas.what: Normalisation η = ξ l_1^{−ν}, which makes η a symmetric matrix [[(1+B²)/D, B],[B, D]].
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of the second GT component (the analogue of choosing f in the commutator subgroup)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine linear-algebra computation of the image of GT-type solutions in a congruence/linear quotient. The answer is an affine Borel group parametrised by a unit and an even element, which matches what specialists would expect; nothing here appears beyond the known picture.
transcription_corrections: In (159), 'S=[-T-]=B' should read 'S=T=B': both S and T equal B, and the T is not struck out.
The heading 'Remarque' at top left is underlined; the page number is 410.
In (160), the subscript is u_ξ (an η overwritten).
